meta.subtitle: ARCALYST keeps compounding and guidance went up, but at 65.9x current-year EPS the shares already price in most of the good news

analystCommentary:
Kiniksa is a one-product commercial story with a pipeline aimed at extending that product's franchise. ARCALYST drives essentially all revenue, the second-quarter 2026 results beat the year-ago quarter by a wide margin, and management raised its 2026 ARCALYST net product revenue guidance in the July 28, 2026 release. The balance sheet carries no debt and the business generates cash.

The problem is the entry price. After a run from the low end of the 52-week range to near its top, the stock trades on a multiple of current-year consensus EPS that already assumes the growth continues for several years. Our Base case sits at the Street low target, our Bear case is a real derating paired with slower earnings, and the probability-weighted fair value clears the price by a margin that is too thin relative to the downside.

We rate KNSA a HOLD. The business is executing well; the valuation leaves little room for a stumble in a company that splits ARCALYST profits evenly with Regeneron, relies on third parties for supply, and does not expect KPL-387 to reach the market before 2028 or 2029.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Kiniksa Pharmaceuticals International, plc is a London-based biopharmaceutical company focused on cardiovascular indications. Its commercial product, ARCALYST, is an IL-1 alpha and IL-1 beta cytokine trap licensed from Regeneron in 2017 and approved by the FDA in March 2021 for recurrent pericarditis and reduction in risk of recurrence in adults and children 12 years and older. ARCALYST is also approved in the United States for CAPS and DIRA.

Kiniksa sells and distributes ARCALYST in the United States through a select network of specialty pharmacies and evenly splits profits on sales, and third-party proceeds, with Regeneron. ARCALYST is currently only approved for sale in the United States, and the company expects to derive substantially all product revenue there for the foreseeable future. Kiniksa reports a single segment.

The pipeline is built around the same IL-1 pathway: KPL-387, a monthly subcutaneous monoclonal antibody in a pivotal Phase 3 trial in recurrent pericarditis, and KPL-1161, a pre-clinical, longer half-life follow-on. Kiniksa has also licensed vixarelimab to Genentech and ARCALYST rights in an Asian territory to Huadong.

thesis.body:
ARCALYST is still growing quickly, with high gross margins, positive free cash flow and no debt, and management raised its 2026 revenue outlook in July. That is the bull case, and the reported numbers support it.

The shares already discount much of it. The stock trades near the top of its 52-week range on a multiple of current-year consensus EPS that needs several more years of strong growth to compress, while half of ARCALYST's profit belongs to Regeneron and the follow-on product is still in Phase 3. Our probability-weighted value sits above the price, but not by enough relative to a real Bear case, so we rate the shares HOLD rather than chase them.

catalysts: Third-quarter 2026 results, as a check on whether ARCALYST is tracking toward the raised full-year guidance.
Enrollment progress in PASTORALE, the pivotal Phase 3 trial of KPL-387 in recurrent pericarditis.
Initiation of a first-in-human Phase 1 trial of KPL-1161, which the company expects by the end of 2026.
Any development, regulatory or sales-based milestone from the Genentech vixarelimab license.
risks: Single-product concentration: ARCALYST is the company's one commercial product.
Supply: the move of ARCALYST drug substance manufacturing to a new contract manufacturer.
Valuation: a high multiple of current-year EPS leaves the shares exposed to any growth slowdown.
Pipeline timing: the lead pipeline antibody is not expected to be commercialized before 2028 or 2029.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Total revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $243.6 million, compared to $156.8 million for the second quarter of 2025, a {+ +55.4% YoY +} increase. The company attributes the quarter's growth to new and repeat prescribers of ARCALYST, which led to a meaningful increase in patients on therapy.

Costs rose with revenue. Total operating expenses were $216.4 million against $136.6 million a year earlier. Collaboration expenses, which are mainly Regeneron's share of ARCALYST profit, reached $88.1 million against $52.4 million, so roughly half of the incremental profit flows to the partner by design. R&D expenses were $40.9 million against $18.8 million, which the company attributes primarily to increased KPL-387 clinical and manufacturing activity and preclinical investment. SG&A was $63.9 million against $46.9 million, attributed to ARCALYST commercialization. Net income was $25.4 million versus $17.8 million, and the Q2'26 operating margin was 11.2%.

On an annual view, FY25 revenue of $677.6M grew +60.1% and the operating margin turned to 11.4% from -10.8% in FY24. Diluted EPS has been uneven: $2.60 in FY22, $0.20 in FY23, a loss in FY24 and $0.75 in FY25, and no source explains the FY22 spike. Gross margin has stayed in a high band, at 88.5% in FY25. The top line is strong, but the even profit split and rising R&D keep operating leverage modest, so earnings grow slower than the revenue headline suggests.
financials.balanceCommentary:
As of June 30, 2026, Kiniksa had $525.9 million of cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments and no debt, according to the second-quarter release. The FY25 year-end figure for cash and short-term investments was $0.4B, so the cash balance has grown during 2026.

Liquidity is ample: the current ratio was 3.79 at FY25 and 3.90 on a trailing basis, and total equity was $0.6B at FY25. The balance sheet is a strength rather than a swing factor; it funds the pivotal Phase 3 trial and the KPL-1161 program without external capital on today's plan. The counterweight is that a debt-free balance sheet does not protect the equity from a valuation reset, which is the main risk we see.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow turned meaningful in FY25 at $136.4M, a 20.1% FCF margin, up from low single-digit margins in FY22 through FY24. Capital spending is small, so operating cash flow and free cash flow move together. The company expects its current operating plan to remain cash flow positive on an annual basis.

Two cautions apply. Second-quarter 2026 operating expenses included $11.6 million of non-cash, share-based compensation, so cash generation flatters per-share economics somewhat. And at the current price the trailing FCF yield is only 3.1%, which says the market is paying for future growth rather than today's cash. Cash flow supports the business but does not by itself support the valuation.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing numbers the shares trade at 77.9x earnings, 53.3x EV/EBITDA and 7.1x sales. The vendor's forward P/E labelled NTM is 65.9x; set against the FY26E consensus EPS of $1.16, that figure is effectively a current-year multiple rather than a true next-twelve-months one. On the FY27E consensus EPS of $1.62 the forward P/E is ~47.2x.

It is not stated whether the consensus EPS estimates are on a GAAP or adjusted basis, so we do not label these forward multiples as GAAP. Peer multiples were not available, so we make no relative comparison.

Even on next year's estimates the stock carries a high earnings multiple. That multiple can hold only if consensus growth is delivered roughly on schedule, which is why the Base case below leans on the Street rather than on multiple expansion.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: ARCALYST keeps adding patients and prescribers, FY26 revenue lands at or above the raised guidance, and PASTORALE progresses on plan. The market rewards the stock at the Street high target of $108.00 over a 12-month horizon.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue tracks consensus and the FY27E EPS of $1.62 stays intact, but the multiple stays roughly where it is rather than expanding. We anchor to the Street low target of $87.00 over a 12-month horizon.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Growth slows, FY27 estimates are cut back toward the FY26E EPS of $1.16, and the market pays roughly the current ~47.2x FY27E multiple on that lower base instead of next year's number. Over 12 months that implies about $55.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We weight Base at 50%, with Bull and Bear at 25% each. The Base case uses the lowest Street target as a checkable anchor rather than the consensus target of $98.00, because the stock has already re-rated sharply over the past year and a further multiple gain is not our central case. The Bull case uses the Street high target, which assumes the growth and pipeline story both hold.

The Bear case is a real downside, not a formality. It pairs weaker earnings with a lower effective multiple, which is how a growth stock usually derates, and it sits well above the 52-week low of $35.20.

On these weights the expected upside clears the BUY hurdle on E, but the reward-to-risk ratio falls well short of the 0.50x the BUY rule requires, because the Bear price sits much further below the current price than the probability-weighted value sits above it. The call is therefore HOLD, and it is not close on reward/risk. Weights reflect what we believe: we think strong execution is more likely than a derating, but not by enough to justify more than a quarter weight on Bull. The target range brackets the Base case and spans from modestly below the current price to the consensus target.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Kiniksa reports one segment, and ARCALYST product revenue is substantially all of it, with FY25 revenue of $677.6M shown as the consolidated total. License and collaboration revenue from Huadong and Genentech is small today: of the $32.0 million Huadong transaction price, $0.2 million had been recognized as of June 30, 2026. The Genentech license could pay up to approximately $600.0 million in contingent payments, of which approximately $570.0 million remains, but those payments are contingent and we place no value on them in our scenarios.

moatFactors.name: Regulatory exclusivity
moatFactors.body: The FDA granted ARCALYST Orphan Drug exclusivity in 2021 for recurrent pericarditis, and the FDA granted KPL-387 Orphan Drug Designation in October 2025. No expiry date is given for these protections, and the 10-K lists the inability to establish and maintain patent and trade secret protection or regulatory exclusivity, and competition from biosimilars, among its commercialization risks.

moatFactors.name: Entrenched prescriber base and long therapy duration
moatFactors.body: Since launch, more than 5,000 prescribers have written ARCALYST prescriptions for recurrent pericarditis, and average total duration of therapy was approximately 3 years as of the end of the second quarter of 2026. Long-duration patients make revenue recurring, but the same 10-K risk list notes that alternative therapies with the same or different mechanisms could compete.

moatFactors.name: Franchise extension in the same indication
moatFactors.body: The Phase 3 antibody targets monthly self-administration in a liquid formulation and KPL-1161 a quarterly profile, against weekly ARCALYST. If they succeed, Kiniksa keeps its patients in-house with more convenient dosing. Both remain investigational, so this factor is a possibility rather than a protection today.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. ARCALYST holds a defined position in a rare indication, with orphan exclusivity, a large prescriber base and long average therapy duration. Against that, Kiniksa owns only half the economics, depends on Regeneron's license and on third-party manufacturers, and no exclusivity end date is given. Durability past the current exclusivity window rests on the Phase 3 antibody reaching the market, which the company expects only in 2028 or 2029.

points: **Raised guidance.** Kiniksa expects 2026 ARCALYST net product revenue of between $980 million and $995 million, compared to prior guidance of between $930 million and $945 million, per the July 28, 2026 release. FY26E consensus revenue of $993.7M sits near the top of that range, so the Street already assumes strong delivery.

**Penetration headroom.** As of the end of the second quarter of 2026, approximately 21% of the 14,000 multiple-recurrence patients were actively on ARCALYST, and the 10-Q estimates a United States prevalent recurrent pericarditis population of approximately 40,000 patients seeking and receiving treatment. The runway is real, though the company does not say what share it expects to reach.

**KPL-387.** PASTORALE, an event-driven randomized withdrawal study enrolling up to approximately 85 participants, began enrolling and dosing patients after Phase 2 data supported the 300 mg monthly dose. The company expects to begin commercializing the antibody in 2028 or 2029, so it is not a near-term revenue driver, and the release cautions that final data may differ from the interval analysis.

**Next year.** Consensus looks for FY27E revenue of $1.2B, which implies continued growth but slower than this year's pace. Whether ARCALYST can sustain growth as penetration rises is the central question for the stock, and it remains open.

**Manufacturing.** In June 2026 the FDA approved Samsung Biologics as the replacement contract manufacturer for ARCALYST drug substance, after a technology transfer Regeneron initiated in 2023. That approval removes one supply uncertainty for growth, though Kiniksa still relies on third parties as the sole source of supply.

management.leadership: Sanj K. Patel is Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, per the July 28, 2026 release. No tenure or biography is available for him or other officers, so we do not characterize the team's track record beyond the reported results. On execution, the second quarter shows the team delivering: guidance went up, PASTORALE started dosing, and the manufacturing transfer cleared FDA approval. The open question is whether the company can carry the same commercial discipline into a second product, which no current data can test.
management.capitalAllocation: The cash flow data show no share repurchases and no dividends in FY21 through FY25, and the dividend yield is 0.00%. Capital goes to the pipeline: higher R&D spending on KPL-387 and KPL-1161, and commercial investment behind ARCALYST. In February 2025 the company discontinued development of abiprubart in Sjogren's Disease and said it would explore strategic alternatives for the asset, which shows some willingness to prune. We consider the reinvestment sensible while ARCALYST funds it, but the forward-looking statements also flag business development as a risk to financial performance, and no deal pipeline is disclosed to assess.
management.governance: According to the proxy statement dated April 16, 2026, all directors other than Sanj K. Patel qualify as independent under Nasdaq listing requirements; Mr. Patel does not because he is the Chief Executive Officer. The proxy states there are no family relationships among directors or executive officers, and that M. Cantey Boyd joined the board in 2024 after a recommendation from an independent director. The combined Chairman and CEO role concentrates authority in one person, which outside holders should weigh against an otherwise independent board.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt dated April 16, 2026 describes four share classes as of its record date: 46,218,660 Class A Shares, 1,795,158 Class B Shares, 12,781,964 Class A1 Shares and 16,057,618 Class B1 Shares. Class A1 and B1 conversions are capped where a holder would beneficially own more than 4.99% of Class A Shares. The excerpt does not include the ownership table itself, so we cannot attribute stakes to any director, officer or outside holder. The multi-class structure also means the vendor's share count should not be over-read.

idiosyncratic: **Single-product dependence.** ARCALYST is Kiniksa's one commercial product and is approved for sale only in the United States. Any slowdown in new patient starts, payor coverage or specialty pharmacy performance would hit revenue directly; the 10-K notes the company currently enjoys largely favorable coverage and seeks to maintain it. Watch quarterly patient and prescriber figures and any change in payor terms.

**Partner economics.** Kiniksa evenly splits ARCALYST profits with Regeneron, and collaboration expenses rise with sales. That caps the share of incremental profit Kiniksa keeps. Track collaboration expenses relative to revenue each quarter.

**Supply.** The forward-looking statements cite reliance on third parties as the sole source of supply of drug substance and drug product. A disruption during the move to Samsung Biologics could interrupt sales. Track any inventory or supply commentary in the 10-Q.

**Clinical and regulatory.** PASTORALE could produce negative, inconclusive or commercially uncompetitive results, and regulators could require additional data, per the release's own cautions. A setback would remove the franchise-extension leg of the thesis. Monitor enrollment updates and the KPL-1161 Phase 1 start.

**Competition.** The 10-K lists competitor products, biosimilars and alternative therapies with the same or different mechanisms among commercialization risks. No specific entrant is named, so the risk is unquantified. Follow any new approvals in recurrent pericarditis.
risks.systemic: Drug pricing and reimbursement policy is the main external risk: the forward-looking statements cite current and future healthcare reforms affecting payment for healthcare products, and orphan-disease pricing depends on payor tolerance. Broader equity sentiment toward high-multiple growth stocks matters too, because the valuation rests on future earnings. The company carries no debt, so interest rate moves affect the shares mainly through the discount rate investors apply. As a London-based company with a United States revenue base, Kiniksa also cites global economic policy uncertainty among its risks.

body: HOLD, with a target range of $70 to $98 over 12 months. Kiniksa is executing well on ARCALYST and its pipeline, and the balance sheet carries no debt. The valuation already reflects that execution, and our scenario analysis does not offer enough upside relative to the Bear case to justify a BUY.

We would turn more constructive if the share price fell meaningfully with the growth path intact, or if 2027 guidance, when issued, comes in clearly above the FY27E consensus revenue. We would turn more cautious if ARCALYST guidance were cut, if the Samsung Biologics transition caused supply disruption, or if PASTORALE were delayed.
